evidence: Film thickness was measured by spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) on Si witness samples u sing a J.A. Woollam variable angle alpha spectrometer. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) was used to analyze film morphology using a Dimension Fastscan (Bruker) in tapping mode. Film phase, strain, and crystallinity were characterized using Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Micro-Raman spectroscopy was conducted on a DXRxi Raman Imaging Microscope (Thermo Scientific) using a 532nm laser with a power of 4 mW and spot size of 0.7um. XRD spectra were acquired on two different systems. XPS spectra were obtained using a Thermo Scientific K -Alpha system. Finally, Cathodoluminescence (CL) was used to study the defectivity of the deposited TiO 2 films. Grazing incidence diffraction (GID) were also measured using a Bruker three -circle platform diffractometer equipped with a PHOTON 100 CMOS detector. High-resolution X-ray diffraction (HRXRD) was used to confirm the presence of the rutile ( 200) peak for films grown at 350 °C.
